principles: Reuse one canonical readiness classification and one shared streaming host runner
Fail closed before automatic execution when unattended readiness is not positively established
Make timeouts observable, bounded, and cleanup-complete
Protect explicit high-authority routing inputs from statistical filtering
Design the full positive/edge/adversarial matrix before implementation
drivers: Avoid duplicate runner semantics across candidate and review paths
Preserve productive long-running hosts after their first output
Keep small changes from escalating to full-corpus review
Minimize new code and review surface

options.name: A: Shared readiness admission plus dual-deadline host_run
pros: Reuses canonical readiness evidence and shared slot lifecycle
Separates startup silence from productive total runtime
Supports deterministic injected-runner and fake-child tests
cons: Requires extending shared runner result/config types
Needs careful compatibility defaults for existing callers

options.name: B: Candidate-handler-local Promise race and kill wrapper
cons: Cannot reliably own or reap the shared host_run child
Risks slot leakage and divergent diagnostics

options.name: C: Lower the existing total timeout only
cons: Kills productive slow hosts and still cannot distinguish startup silence
Does not enforce positive unattended readiness
Does not solve cleanup diagnostics or candidate specificity acceptance

chosen: A: Shared readiness admission plus dual-deadline host_run
rationale: Option A closes the actual execution boundary while preserving one canonical process lifecycle. Candidate routing will consume positive unattended readiness before spawn and pass a startup watchdog into host_run; host_run remains the only owner of child kill, close settlement, output observation, and slot release. Existing document-frequency work is retained and completed with relevance-aware escalation and artifact/mode tests.

preMortem.scenario: A legitimate launcher emits no early bytes and is killed as silent
preMortem.trigger: Startup budget is shorter than the launcher-specific valid startup envelope
preMortem.consequence: Usable unattended capacity is falsely rejected
preMortem.mitigation: Use configurable launcher-aware defaults, clear startup timer on first stdout or stderr byte, and test a delayed-but-productive child independently from total timeout

preMortem.scenario: The child is killed but the host-run concurrency slot remains held
preMortem.trigger: Startup timeout settles outside the existing try/finally release path
preMortem.consequence: Later hosts are blocked and the workflow appears deadlocked
preMortem.mitigation: Keep timeout ownership inside the shared runner and assert a new run immediately reacquires capacity after startup and total timeout paths

preMortem.scenario: A readiness probe reports supported but actual execution still blocks
preMortem.trigger: Authentication or session state changes between probe and proposal spawn
preMortem.consequence: Automatic routing waits until timeout despite admission
preMortem.mitigation: Treat readiness as necessary but not sufficient; retain startup watchdog on the actual child and emit distinct stale-readiness or no-output diagnostics

preMortem.scenario: Frequency filtering removes an explicit required source
preMortem.trigger: A common term also appears in relatedDocs, exact paths, registry refs, or bound reviewer evidence
preMortem.consequence: Relevant requirements are omitted from review
preMortem.mitigation: Materialize explicit sources as direct candidates before statistical filtering and test each protected source category at document frequency above the threshold

preMortem.scenario: Raw hit overflow still forces broad review even though omitted hits cannot affect ranking
preMortem.trigger: Truncation is classified without comparing omitted relevance to the candidate cutoff
preMortem.consequence: Tiny changes again demand full-corpus reads
preMortem.mitigation: Escalate only for cutoff ties or omitted scores at or above the deterministic relevance floor, and record the exact query group and cutoff cause

preMortem.scenario: Shadow mode emits enforce-style STOP guidance
preMortem.trigger: Artifact status and renderer use different rollout-mode predicates
preMortem.consequence: Nonblocking rollout behaves like a hard gate
preMortem.mitigation: Bind mode through handler, artifact, renderer, and gate tests; assert shadow records metrics without STOP, warn advises, and enforce alone blocks
